description:
What Will Happen to Earth When the Sun Dies?

Episode 59 of a daily journey through the universe. ☀️
How the Sun will die: in about 5 billion years it runs low on hydrogen, swells into a red giant that swallows Mercury and Venus, sheds its outer layers into a glowing nebula, and ends as a white dwarf about the size of Earth.

segments.text: One day the Sun will die. What happens to Earth, and everything on it?
Our Sun is about four and a half billion years old. It's about halfway through its life.
segments.headline: Halfway through

segments.text: In its core, it fuses hydrogen into helium. Eventually, the hydrogen in the core will run low.
segments.headline: Running low

segments.text: That happens in about five billion years.
Then the Sun will swell into a red giant, hundreds of times wider than it is today.
segments.headline: A red giant

segments.text: Mercury and Venus will be swallowed. Earth may be too, or it may survive as a scorched rock. Scientists still debate it.
segments.headline: What about Earth?

segments.text: Even before that, in about a billion years, the brightening Sun will make Earth too hot for oceans.
Near the end, the Sun will gently blow off its outer layers into space, making a glowing shell called a planetary nebula, like this one.
segments.headline: A glowing shell

segments.text: What's left will be its hot core: a white dwarf, about the size of Earth, but with half the Sun's mass.
segments.headline: A white dwarf

segments.text: A teaspoon of it would weigh several tons. It will slowly cool and fade for trillions of years.
